technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, which is designed to improve the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud. Meanwhile, Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, raising questions about the future of human employees. In other news, a former Plaud executive has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background, and Fitbit has officially launched the Fitbit Edge, a fitness tracker for those who want notifications without a screen.

finance.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. The launch of the India Market Access portal in September 2025 was a significant step forward in this initiative.

However, global uncertainty has impacted the market and investor sentiment remains cautious. Benchmark indices have faced a decline, with the Nifty index under pressure.

In other news, a resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher.

Meanwhile, Indian hospital stocks have slipped after the Supreme Court of India highlighted troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals.

politics.summary: The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for a SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a Mumbai protest were detained. Meanwhile, Donald Trump has called the US electoral process "corrupt", citing an Indian election that didn't happen.
